title: Mid-procedure
stem:
You are an F2 doctor in the Emergency Department. You are halfway through a lumbar puncture, with the needle in place and fluid collecting slowly.

A nurse tells you that a patient in resus has dropped his blood pressure to 78/40 and is becoming drowsy.
instruction: Choose the 3 most appropriate actions to take in this situation.

options.text: Remove the needle immediately and go to resus.
options.brief: Abandoning the procedure isn't necessary when others can attend.
options.detailed: This puts the deteriorating patient first, which is the right instinct, but others can attend immediately, and abandoning the procedure exposes this patient to a repeat.

options.text: Ask the nurse to give a fluid bolus and call you back in ten minutes.
options.brief: A drowsy, hypotensive patient needs a doctor now.
options.detailed: Fluids may be needed, but a drowsy patient with low blood pressure needs immediate medical assessment, not a delayed call back.

options.text: Ask the patient having the lumbar puncture whether you can leave for a few minutes.
options.brief: Not a fair question to put to a patient mid-procedure.
options.detailed: This puts the patient in an impossible position and doesn't solve the problem of who sees the patient in resus.

options.text: Ask the nurse to monitor the patient in resus until you've finished.
options.brief: Monitoring isn't enough for a deteriorating patient.
options.detailed: The patient needs a doctor's assessment now, not just monitoring.

options.text: Ask the nurse to call the ED registrar to resus straight away.
options.brief: A deteriorating patient needs senior help now.
options.detailed: You can't leave a patient mid-procedure safely, but the deteriorating patient needs a doctor now. The registrar can attend immediately.

options.text: Complete the lumbar puncture as quickly as safely possible.
options.brief: Leaving a needle in place, or removing it hastily, risks harm.
options.detailed: Abandoning the procedure would mean starting again later and could harm the patient. Completing it safely, without rushing unduly, lets you help in resus soon.

options.text: Go to resus as soon as you have finished.
options.brief: Your help may still be needed.
options.detailed: Once the procedure is complete, joining the team in resus means you can help with the sick patient.

options.text: Continue the lumbar puncture at your normal pace, as you are committed to it.
options.brief: Ignores the urgency of the other patient.
options.detailed: Completing the procedure is right, but the other patient needs help to be arranged now.

explanation.issue: This tests how you respond to an emergency when you can't safely leave the patient in front of you.
explanation.keyDetails: You are mid-procedure. The other patient is hypotensive and drowsy. Senior help is available.
explanation.reasoning: [E] gets a senior to the sick patient, [F] finishes safely, and [G] brings you to help afterwards. The distractors abandon the procedure ([A]), delay assessment ([B], [D]), burden the patient ([C]), or ignore the urgency ([H]).
explanation.competing: [A] is the tempting option, but others can attend immediately, so abandoning the procedure isn't necessary.

references.title: Good medical practice
references.note: Domain 1, prioritising patients and asking for help.
